Our story

Five years, one brick, several materials.

SeaBrick began in 2021 as an idea about kelp and coastlines. The brick has been through more than twenty versions and its material three stages since. This is the short version; the journal has the long one.

2021

An idea called Kelp Island

A research document about building coastal infrastructure from kelp becomes a project. The first pitch, in September 2021, already describes coastal cities building out onto the water. In August the idea changes from a ceramic block to a compressed plant-fibre brick formed in a mould.

Origin
Feb 2022

SeaBrick Society incorporated

A federal not-for-profit corporation is formed to hold the standard and the research record. Its purpose: to promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.

Society
Jan–Mar 2022

First designs and first prints

A 3D designer turns eight months of sketches into a brick; 3DSMITH in Vancouver prints the first ten-centimetre bricks within days. The first patent application is filed on 10 March 2022, with drawings of a whole family of shapes.

ShapePatents
2022

Kelp fibre composites at UBC

Six UBC Materials Engineering students take SeaBrick on as a Capstone project and make a kelp composite stronger than concrete. Its density, close to water, leads to a hollow-core brick.

Materials
2023

Kelpstone

A sponsored research agreement with UBC's BioProducts Institute. The composite is named Kelpstone; small specimens test at around three times the compressive strength of concrete at half the weight. Three more Capstone teams join in the autumn. A small manufacturing space is leased on Venables Street.

Materials
2023

Recognition

Accepted to the Third Derivative climate accelerator. Climate Spotlight winner at the Ocean Impact Pitchfest in Sydney. Nominated by Ashoka for the 2024 Earthshot Prize.

Society
Oct 2023 – Sep 2024

The hinge-lock

The tongue-and-bump locking system is replaced by a hinge-lock concept, developed with 3D printing advisor Brady Kirk and designer Xiaoyuan Geng, and declared final for patent purposes in September 2024.

Shape
2024

Perth, sargassum and a waterproofing grant

Materials work continues in Western Australia with a simpler process; sargassum proves to work as well as kelp. Canada's Ocean Supercluster funds a validation study of a mineral-based waterproofing method. Three further patent applications are filed on kelp processing and farming.

MaterialsPatents
2025

Flax, hemp and a float test

With seaweed fibre unobtainable at scale, flax and hemp from the Prairies are tested and perform at least as well. An eight-inch hexagonal brick moulded in two halves is float-tested in February. UBC students run the waterproofing study.

Materials
Aug–Dec 2025

The component brick

The brick is redesigned in SolidWorks as a set of simpler moulded parts that assemble into one unit, solving the mould problem. A provisional patent on the new design is filed on 9 December 2025.

ShapePatents
Jan–Jun 2026

A thousand model bricks

About a thousand toy-scale bricks in some fifty types are printed. On 13 June 2026 friends and advisors spend an afternoon building with them to choose the first brick set.

ShapeCommunity
Jul–Oct 2026

Mineral foam and fibre

The materials strategy moves to a mineral foam core with a dense mineral shell and short plant-fibre reinforcement. A marine validation programme is designed around density, water uptake, shrinkage and demoulding. In September the first production-oriented brick design, made for a compression press, is completed.

MaterialsShape

The materials thread

Three stages, one direction: a material that floats, lasts in seawater and costs the planet very little.

2021–23Kelp fibre composite ("Kelpstone"), with UBC
2025Flax and hemp fibre composites
2026 →Mineral foam core, mineral shell, plant-fibre reinforcement

Where the strategy stands

The shape thread

Square slab, a family of shapes, a hollow two-part brick, the hinge-lock, the component brick, a thousand toy bricks, and the final SeaBrick. The evolution page shows each generation; the journal tells the story.

People

The work has been carried by a founder, a changing cast of directors and CEOs, UBC faculty and students, independent engineers, 3D-printing and design collaborators, patent counsel and a community of advisors and supporters. Named contributors appear in the journal articles where their work is described.

SeaBrick Society is a not-for-profit corporation incorporated in Canada in 2022 to promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.
